title: TESS sector 91 aperture tests recover at most 1.5 percent of 200 ppm boxes at six times the early depth scatter
abstract: We test shallow-dip sensitivity at HD 139139 with public TESS sector 91 pixels. Three aperture radii and three box durations give 0 to 1.48 percent recovery for 200 ppm signals at known later times, at six times the early robust depth scatter. Three times that scatter gives 0.84 to 41.35 percent recovery. These are conditional aperture-flux tests, not pixel-level or blind-search completeness. One selected 7-hour feature has strong aperture, baseline and background dependence and lies near a quality-data gap. We do not confirm a new dip or planet, infer that the K2 dip process stopped, or identify a physical cause. Code, aggregate results, figures, exact source hashes and external retrieval steps are included.
